**Impact:** Information Disclosure ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** x64, Arm64 ## Affected Packages ### Standalone Aspire CLI Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- Aspire CLI ([Aspire.Cli](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli)) | >= 13.2.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.linux-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.linux-x64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.linux-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.linux-arm64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.linux-musl-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.linux-musl-x64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.osx-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.osx-x64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.osx-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.osx-arm64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 ### Aspire CLI npm packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [@microsoft/aspire-cli](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-x64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-x64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-arm64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-arm64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-musl-x64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-musl-x64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-x64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-x64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-arm64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-arm64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 The affected component is the Aspire CLI's deprecated MCP configuration scanner, which ships in the CLI packages listed above. If installed as a .NET tool, update the Aspire.Cli package. If installed using npm, update @microsoft/aspire-cli to version 13.6.5 or later; its platform-specific dependency must also resolve to version 13.6.5 or later. Otherwise update the CLI through its installation method. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). items.summary:
### Impact

Crafted payloads targeting frameworks supporting React Server Components can lead to remote code execution. This only affects extremely rare cases where responses transport multiple typed arrays and an attacker-controlled value.

Updating immediately is recommended.

The vulnerability exists in versions 19.0.0 through 19.0.8, 19.1.0 through 19.1.9, 19.2.0 through 19.2.8 and 19.3.0 of:

- react-server-dom-webpack
- react-server-dom-parcel
- react-server-dom-turbopack

### Patches

Fixes were back ported to versions 19.0.09, 19.1.10, 19.2.9, and 19.3.1.

If applications are using any of the above packages please upgrade to any of the fixed versions immediately.

If an app’s React code does not use a server, the app is not affected by this vulnerability. If an app does not use a framework, bundler, or bundler plugin that supports React Server Components, the app is not affected by this vulnerability.

items.summary:
### Impact

0.31.0 fixed GHSA-6f4g-xm8v-pgv6, where text from a Compose file became GitHub Actions workflow commands in compose-lint's output. The fix escapes the command openers in compose-lint's own output, but not in the argument parser's error messages. When a repository path reaches compose-lint's arguments without a `--` before it, the argument parser prints it raw in its error message. That includes a carriage return, which the runner treats as a line break, so a command can also start a new line there.

A pull request can therefore create annotations, fold or hide parts of the job log, or issue other commands the runner accepts, when CI runs compose-lint over it, before anyone reviews it. The pass/fail result is not changed.

Affected setups pass repository paths to compose-lint without a `--` before them: the pre-commit hook when `args:` is set without the documented trailing `--`, or the `compose-lint` package or Docker image called that way in a workflow. The pre-commit hook's default configuration passes `--` and is not affected. The GitHub Action turns command processing off around each compose-lint run, so it is not affected.

Found during an internal pre-1.0 security review. It was first published as part of GHSA-r7j4-crjv-h467, together with four other gaps in the same fix. Each gap now has its own advisory.

**Docker image.** `composelint/compose-lint` tag 0.31.0 and the matching minor tag are affected, as was `latest` while it pointed to 0.31.0.

Releases before 0.31.0 are covered by GHSA-6f4g-xm8v-pgv6.

### Patches

Fixed in 0.32.0. The argument parser's messages go through the same sanitizer as the rest of compose-lint's output.

### Workarounds

- Upgrade to 0.32.0 or later.
- End the pre-commit hook's `args:` with `--`, and put `--` before file paths when calling compose-lint directly.
- On GitHub Actions, use the `tmatens/compose-lint` Action, or bracket the compose-lint step with `::stop-commands::<random token>` and `::<token>::`, as the Action does.

### Reproduction

On compose-lint 0.31.0 on a GitHub-hosted runner (runner 2.337.0), `compose-lint '--##[warning]X/compose.yml'` with no `--` creates an annotation. The same path after `--` creates none. The `composelint/compose-lint:0.31.0` image produces byte-identical output to the package.
items.title: compose-lint: File paths embedded in pull requests can inject CI workflow commands through command-line error messages

items.summary:
### Impact

In Action tags v0.30.0 and v0.31.0, when `sarif-file:` names a file in a subdirectory that can't be created, the Action prints the directory's resolved path in an error message. In v0.31.0 that message is outside the window in which the Action turns command processing off, and v0.30.0 has no such window. A pull request can commit a symlink on that path to a directory whose name contains a newline followed by a command.

A pull request can therefore create annotations, fold or hide parts of the job log, or issue other commands the runner accepts, when CI runs compose-lint over it, before anyone reviews it. The pass/fail result is not changed.

Only the Action is affected, and only when `sarif-file:` points into a subdirectory. The documented setup, `sarif-file: results.sarif` at the repository root, is not affected. The `compose-lint` package, the pre-commit hook and the Docker image do not print this message.

Found during an internal pre-1.0 security review. It was first published as part of GHSA-r7j4-crjv-h467, together with four other gaps in the same fix. Each gap now has its own advisory.

### Patches

Fixed in 0.32.0. The SARIF-directory error names the `sarif-file:` input as written.

### Workarounds

- Upgrade to 0.32.0 or later.
- Keep `sarif-file` at the workspace root, for example `sarif-file: results.sarif`.

### Reproduction

On a GitHub-hosted runner (runner 2.337.0), the Action at v0.31.0 with `sarif-file: out/reports/results.sarif`, where `out` is a committed symlink to a directory named `d\n::warning::X` that contains a regular file `reports`, creates an annotation. With `sarif-file` at the repository root it creates none.
items.title: compose-lint: Workflow command injection through SARIF-directory errors triggered by pull request symlinks
